source.title: How Edge of Stability Hinders SCAFFOLD in Federated Optimization
source.authors: Anant Khandelwal; M. Crawshaw; Ming-Rui Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures federated training loss, sharpness, and update misalignment in image-classification networks. Its training setup and outcomes bear on whether training reaches low loss, but it does not test random initialization or training classification error as specified by the versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports federated training losses and optimization dynamics, but not training classification error or the effects of random initialization, width, shortcuts, or normalization. Loss values are included as results bearing on the broad training claim; they do not establish classification-error outcomes. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's progressive-sharpening and Edge of Stability component in a new setting: full-batch federated optimization. Sections 4.1–4.2 report sharpness and loss trajectories directly, although none of the extracted rows captures these results. Training-loss comparisons alone do not test V1's classification-error claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but EoS is setting-dependent: both algorithms show EoS-like dynamics on CIFAR-10, while easier tasks often avoid sustained EoS. The authors propose that high sharpness compromises SCAFFOLD's global-gradient estimates and helps explain its performance relative to FedAvg. Their correlations and dataset comparisons support a proposed mechanism rather than establish causation.
record.recipe_differences: Federated full-batch training with FedAvg and SCAFFOLD; measures training loss, sharpness, and update misalignment. It does not use the original claim's single-model benchmark recipes or report classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Sharpness behavior and algorithm-relative training loss vary with dataset, learning rate, heterogeneity, communication interval, network depth, and dataset size. The authors report that the equilibrium sharpness is inversely proportional to learning rate; heterogeneity has a smaller effect, and communication interval has almost no effect. CIFAR-10 and MNIST show different relative training-loss outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: FedAvg has lower final CIFAR-10 loss in all six table settings; SCAFFOLD has lower MNIST loss in all six. Learning rates were tuned separately.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative training-loss performance of FedAvg and SCAFFOLD depends on the dataset and associated optimization regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Detrended sharpness–update-misalignment correlations are 0.544–0.813 for SCAFFOLD and −0.157–0.162 for FedAvg.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SCAFFOLD's global-gradient estimation error tracks sharpness during these federated CIFAR-10 trajectories, whereas FedAvg's error is comparatively unrelated.

record.problems: Experiments use full-batch gradients and small architectures because of hardware limits; the paper notes this limits the work's scope. Most training runs are single trajectories. Some reported comparisons average three random seeds with min/max error bars, but Table 1 and Table 2 report no uncertainty. The paper does not measure classification error, which limits its relevance to the supplied versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 2 results are recorded separately for each algorithm, dataset, size, and depth. Appendix figure-only trajectories are not separately extracted because the main reported numeric and textual outcomes are represented in the table rows and excerpts.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and sufficiently large networks trained under the specified SGD/Adam conditions.
Teacher–student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and student-width interventions.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized networks and comparisons with identity shortcuts, special initialization, or Fixup.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Squared-loss catapult recovery above the initial linearized stability limit; systematic recovery-versus-divergence boundaries; divergence despite starting below that limit. The reported divergence at learning rate 0.05 does not establish its position relative to an initial stability threshold.
Batch-normalization interventions and comparisons with otherwise matched unnormalized or Fixup networks.

missing.what: Direct V5 rows for progressive sharpening, equilibrium behavior, and associated loss oscillations. For SCAFFOLD's CIFAR-10 MLP at η=0.005, loss becomes non-monotonic after about 500 steps as local sharpness equilibrates near 1250. Record the distinction between local and global sharpness.

Direct V5 rows for the modified equilibrium threshold: doubling η from 0.005 to 0.01 approximately halves equilibrium sharpness; FedAvg equilibrium decreases from about 550 to 350 as heterogeneity increases from 0 to 0.9; communication interval has almost no effect.

Direct V5 rows for easier-task exceptions: MNIST sharpness declines toward small values without sustained EoS; FashionMNIST has mixed trajectories, including decline, no rise, and some threshold persistence.
missing.locator: Sections 4.1 and 4.3; Figure 5; Appendix B, Figures 6–7

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. All extracted table numbers match the supplied text. The reader overlooked V5's explicit full-batch Edge of Stability component. Although rows_left_out mentions omitted figure trajectories, the main textual findings about equilibrium thresholds and task exceptions are not represented by the table rows and require extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Reports training loss on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, but not training classification error, random or corrupted labels, initialization, model size thresholds, or the listed SGD/Adam benchmark conditions.

relationships.condition: Full-batch FedAvg and SCAFFOLD on CIFAR-10, with CNNs and MLPs
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict, missing direct rows: Sections 4.1–4.2 report sharpening followed by loss oscillations, but equilibrium sharpness differs from the usual 2/η threshold and depends on heterogeneity; local and global sharpness can behave differently.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpening preceded loss oscillations, but equilibrium sharpness differed from 2/η, depended on heterogeneity, and could differ between local and global models.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Full-batch FedAvg and SCAFFOLD on CIFAR-10, with CNNs and MLPs
source_check.reason: Sections 4.1–4.2 report sharpening and non-monotonic loss, but sharpness does not equilibrate around the usual 2/η threshold. Heterogeneity affects equilibrium sharpness, and global sharpness can continue increasing while local sharpness equilibrates.

relationships.condition: Full-batch federated training on MNIST and FashionMNIST
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict, missing direct rows: Section 4.1 and Appendix B report sharpness declining before sustained equilibration in many easier-task settings, with monotonic or eventually monotonic loss; EoS is conditional on the task.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness often declined before sustained equilibration, while loss decreased monotonically or eventually became monotonic.

source_check.reason: Section 4.1 and Appendix B report declining sharpness without sustained equilibration in easier settings, often with monotonic or eventually monotonic loss. Some FashionMNIST settings retain a sharpness threshold, supporting a conditional qualification.
